# GEO report: trailhead

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

Bash was denied, so I read the 8 tracked files with the Read tool. That covers every file in the project. Everything below is read from code.

## Code score: 46–54/100, At risk

Confidence: High (checked 21 of 23 points).
How it's calculated: low = 10.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 46. High = (10.5 + 2) ÷ 23 × 100 = 54.

Trailhead is a Nuxt app with server rendering switched off, so crawlers that don't run JavaScript get an empty page. The `/guides` page is blocked from indexing by a server header, even though your sitemap lists it. The one unknown is the canonical link, which depends on which domain you want to use.

I sampled `/` and `/guides`. `/admin` is deliberately `noindex` and disallowed in `robots.txt`, so I left it out as an intentional choice. I assumed you want search and AI search tools to find the public pages, because there is no `geo.config.json`.

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Turn server rendering back on
- **Why it matters:** Many crawlers read only the HTML the server first sends. With server rendering off, `/` and `/guides` arrive as an empty shell, so those crawlers see no content.
- **Where:** `nuxt.config.ts:2`
- **What the code says:** `ssr: false,`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 59–67 (GEO-003 earns its full 3 points).

### 2. Make the `Sitemap:` line in robots.txt an absolute URL
- **Why it matters:** Crawlers expect a full address for the sitemap, and a relative path may be ignored. They would then not find your page list through `robots.txt`.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:4`
- **What the code says:** `Sitemap: /sitemap.xml`
- **Size:** Small. The sitemap itself already uses `https://trailhead.example/`, so use `https://trailhead.example/sitemap.xml` if that is your real domain.
- **Score after this:** 54–63 on its own (GEO-011 earns 2 points).

### 3. Stop `/guides` from sending a noindex header
- **Why it matters:** `/guides` is in your sitemap and linked from the home page, but the server tells search engines not to index it. These signals contradict each other, and the page is the one that holds your trail guide content.
- **Where:** `server/middleware/headers.ts:3`
- **What the code says:** `setResponseHeader(event, 'X-Robots-Tag', 'noindex');`
- **Size:** Small. Remove that middleware block, or take `/guides` out of the sitemap if hiding it is intended.
- **Score after this:** 51–59 on its own (GEO-014 earns the full 3 points, up from 1.5).

Two more Problems are not in the top three:
- **GEO-012:** every page shares one title and description.
- **GEO-016:** `/guides` is reachable only through a button.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and within size limits | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt` is plain text, valid lines, tiny |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers have the access your policy intends | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt:1-2` only disallows `/admin` |
| GEO-014 | Sitemap-listed and linked routes are indexable | Problem | Not run | 1 of 2 routes clear. `/guides` has `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` at `server/middleware/headers.ts:3` |
| GEO-015 | One absolute canonical on the declared origin | Can't tell | Not run | No canonical anywhere, and no declared origin. The sitemap uses `trailhead.example` |
| GEO-003 | Primary content is in server HTML | Problem | Not run | Site-wide, `nuxt.config.ts:2` has `ssr: false,` |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD parses and is complete | Not applicable | Not run | No JSON-LD in the code |
| GEO-011 | Valid sitemap that is discoverable | Problem | Not run | Site-wide. The sitemap is valid, but `public/robots.txt:4` has a relative `Sitemap:` line |
| GEO-012 | Title, description and html lang | Problem | Not run | 0 of 2 routes clear. `lang` is set at `nuxt.config.ts:5`, but `app/app.vue:2` gives every page the title `Trailhead` and `nuxt.config.ts:6` gives every page one description |
| GEO-016 | Key routes reachable through real links | Problem | Not run | `pages/index.vue:8` has `<button @click="router.push('/guides')">`, and nothing else links to `/guides` |
| GEO-017 | Snippet limits don't conflict with AI-search inclusion | Clear | Not run | No `nosnippet` or `max-snippet:0` in `server/middleware/headers.ts` or the page metadata |
| GEO-002 | Basic accessibility checks | Clear | Not run | Read all 3 pages. There are no images, and the one button has text |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | Not run | No mobile app declared |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only) | Not applicable | Not run | No `llms.txt` found. This is never scored |
| GEO-102 | App structured data (information only) | Not applicable | Not run | Not an app project. This is never scored |

## Can't tell from code

- **GEO-015 canonical:** no page emits a canonical link, and no domain is declared. Tell me your real domain, for example whether it is `https://trailhead.example`, and I can settle this. A fix would then add one absolute canonical per page.
- **GEO-014 and GEO-017 headers:** a CDN or host could add headers the repository doesn't show.
- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>` to check real crawlers against their published addresses.

## Outside GEO

None noticed.

## Assumptions

- You want search and AI search tools to find the public pages (`/` and `/guides`).
- `/admin` is meant to stay hidden, so its `noindex` and `Disallow` are intentional.
- There is no `geo.config.json`, so I used defaults.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
